stem: A pediatric solid-organ recipient develops fever without an obvious source two weeks after transplant. Which initial evaluation aligns with standard references?

options.text: Septic workup including CBC with differential, blood and urine cultures, metabolic panel, and assessment for latent CMV and EBV
No laboratory evaluation because fever is expected and never requires workup
Isolated cosmetic wound inspection without cultures or laboratory studies
Permanent cessation of all immunosuppression before any assessment

explanation.rationale_correct: When no fever source is immediately identified in a pediatric solid-organ recipient, a septic workup is required including CBC with differential, blood and urine cultures, complete metabolic panel, and assessment for latent viruses such as CMV and EBV.

rationale_incorrect.B: Fever evaluation includes thorough history, examination, and septic workup when no source is identified.
rationale_incorrect.C: Evaluation requires laboratory and culture data rather than inspection alone.
rationale_incorrect.D: Fever prompts diagnostic evaluation and team management rather than unilateral immunosuppression cessation.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 17, Pediatric Populations → Infections Principles → C.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: septic workup is required, including a. CBC with differential b. Blood and urine cultures c. Complete metabolic panel d. Assessment for latent viruses (CMV, EBV)

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 17 → Infections Principles → C. (septic workup with CBC, cultures, metabolic panel, CMV/EBV assessment when fever source not identified); PDF p. 944 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Eighth 030100 item; seventh pediatric recipient in bank; pediatric fever-workup angle distinct from urinary-leak labs (cctc-3034) and cholangitis pattern (cctc-3039); anchor verified on Cupples p. 944.

stem: During long-term follow-up of a solid-organ recipient, which malignancy risk counseling point aligns with standard complication references?

options.text: Skin cancer is the most common post-transplant malignancy, with risk markedly higher than the general population
Immunosuppression eliminates malignancy risk after the first post-transplant year
Post-transplant malignancy never affects long-term survival
Only pediatric recipients develop post-transplant skin cancer

explanation.rationale_correct: Post-transplant malignancy is the second most common cause of late mortality; skin cancer is the most common post-transplant malignancy with risk up to 20-fold higher than the general population.

rationale_incorrect.B: Immunosuppression increases malignancy risk rather than eliminating it after one year.
rationale_incorrect.C: Post-transplant malignancy is a major late mortality cause requiring ongoing surveillance and prevention teaching.
rationale_incorrect.D: Skin cancer risk after transplant applies to solid-organ recipients broadly, not pediatric recipients alone.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 12, Long-Term Outcomes → F. Posttransplant malignancy → 2.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Skin cancer is the most common cause of posttransplant malignancy with risk up to 20fold higher than general population

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 12 → F. Posttransplant malignancy → 2. (skin cancer most common post-transplant malignancy; markedly elevated risk); PDF p. 674 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Sixth 030400 item; skin-cancer long-term complication angle distinct from post-transplant diabetes incidence (cctc-3028) and malignancy-prevention combo (cctc-3043); anchor verified on Cupples p. 674.

stem: A recipient was discharged yesterday after solid-organ transplantation. Which post-discharge coordination step aligns with standard references?

options.text: Call the patient the day after discharge to answer questions and review medications
Defer all contact until the one-year anniversary visit
Avoid medication review because discharge teaching is never reinforced
Transfer all follow-up solely to the pharmacy with no transplant team contact

explanation.rationale_correct: Because the initial discharge event may be overwhelming, coordinators should call the patient the day after discharge to answer questions and review medications.

rationale_incorrect.B: Early post-discharge contact is recommended the day after discharge rather than waiting a year.
rationale_incorrect.C: Medication review is a key purpose of the early post-discharge call.
rationale_incorrect.D: The transplant team remains involved in early post-discharge coordination alongside other providers.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → C. Posttransplant Phase → 2.a.

stem: A recipient on mycophenolate mofetil (MMF) is prescribed a proton pump inhibitor after transplant. What discharge medication counseling is MOST important?

options.text: PPI use with MMF may lower mycophenolic acid levels and increase rejection risk if doses are not adjusted
PPIs always increase MMF levels and mandate immediate graft removal
PPI and MMF interactions never affect immunosuppression monitoring
MMF must be stopped permanently whenever any antacid is prescribed

explanation.rationale_correct: Proton pump inhibitors combined with MMF may lower mycophenolic acid levels and lead to rejection if immunosuppression medications are not adjusted, so team coordination is required.

rationale_incorrect.B: The concern is lowered mycophenolic acid levels and rejection risk, not automatic graft removal.
rationale_incorrect.C: Drug interactions between PPIs and MMF can affect immunosuppression efficacy and require monitoring.
rationale_incorrect.D: Management involves team review and possible dose adjustment rather than permanent MMF cessation for every PPI prescription.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 4, Immunosuppression → D. Medications to manage GI symptoms → 4.

references.locator: Ch. 4 → D. Medications to manage GI symptoms → 4. (PPI with MMF may lower mycophenolic acid levels and increase rejection risk if not adjusted); PDF p. 161 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).
